title: Living faith applies the whole Word practically — not Gospel promises only
source_text: LXXVIII. Denique sunt qui existimant applicationem istam, per quam viva & salvifica fides ab historica & mortua distinguitur, restringendam non esse ad promissiones Evangelii, quanquam illae sint potissimum & praecipuum illius objectum; sed fideles per veram illam fidem qua salvantur & justificantur, non solum sibi applicare promissiones gratiae, sed & caetera quae continet Dei verbum; quodque, scilicet, suo modo. Istam vero applicationem in eo consistere, quod vere fidelis omnia quae verbo Dei continentur practice considerat, & ad actionem atque usum suum peculiarem refert. Ita credit, verbi causa, Evangelii promissionibus de remissione peccatorum, de felicitate & gloria aeterna, ut in istis summum suum bonum & beatitudinem, ad quam ipsi sit totis viribus aspirandum, sitam esse firmiter & efficaciter judicet: Ita fidem adhibet Redemptionis nostrae mysteriis, ut in iis consolationem, & pacem conscientiae sibi quaerendam plane existimet: denique sic divina praecepta considerat, ut secundum ista sibi vitam esse exigendam certo apud se constituat, & constanter proponat.
pass_a_gloss: Finally there are those who think that that application by which living and saving faith is distinguished from historical and dead faith is not to be restricted to the promises of the Gospel, although those are chiefly and principally its object; but that the faithful by that true faith by which they are saved and justified apply to themselves not only the promises of grace, but also the other things which God's word contains — each, namely, in its own way. And that this application consists in this, that the truly faithful person practically considers all things contained in God's word, and refers them to his own peculiar action and use. So he believes, for example, the Gospel promises of remission of sins, of happiness and eternal glory, so that he firmly and efficaciously judges that in these his highest good and blessedness is placed, to which he must aspire with all his strength: so he applies faith to the mysteries of our Redemption, that he plainly thinks consolation and peace of conscience are to be sought for himself in them: finally he so considers the divine precepts that he certainly lays down with himself, and constantly proposes, that life is to be lived by him according to these.
pass_b_english: Some: the application that marks living saving faith vs historical/dead is not limited to Gospel promises — though those are its chief object.
True faith applies grace-promises and the rest of God’s Word, each in its own way.
Practically: refer everything in the Word to one’s own action and use.
Promises → judge highest good and blessedness there; redemption mysteries → seek consolation and conscience-peace; precepts → resolve to live by them.
